purpose: Wording and morphology rules for requirements validation
description: Defines all lexical, grammatical, and structural rules applied during requirements analysis and rewriting. Loaded at runtime by arp4754_rules.py. Combines the original term-level rules with the richer bad-practice taxonomy from the project wording guide.

mandatory_modal_verb.note: The only acceptable modal for binding requirements per ARP4754A and DO-178C writing conventions.

weak_modal_verbs.description: Modal verbs that express obligation weaker than 'shall'. Their presence in a binding requirement is a wording defect (REQ-R03, severity LOW).

verbs.note: Conditional — not suitable for binding requirements.
Capability — use 'shall be capable of' for binding statements.
Non-standard in ARP4754A context — replace with 'shall'.
Expresses intent or future state, not a binding obligation.

ambiguous_terms.description: Vague, subjective, or unmeasurable terms that make a requirement unverifiable (REQ-C02, REQ-V02, REQ-V03, severity HIGH). Organised by category for traceability to the project wording guide.

performance_speed.note: Specify a numeric latency, throughput, or response time with unit and tolerance.

quantitative_approximation.note: Specify an exact value ± tolerance (e.g. '100 ms ± 5 ms').

conditional_applicability.note: State the applicability condition explicitly using IF/WHEN/WHILE/WHERE.

subjective_quality_judgment.note: Replace with a measurable acceptance threshold or objective criterion.

performance_attributes.note: Decompose into measurable sub-requirements (e.g. MTBF for 'reliable', fault-recovery time for 'robust').

usability_attributes.note: Specify a measurable usability criterion (e.g. task completion time, error rate).

optimization_terms.note: Specify the target value or bound (e.g. 'shall not exceed X' instead of 'minimize').

state_classification.note: Define the specific operating condition explicitly (e.g. 'during cruise phase' instead of 'normal').

scale_references.note: Specify a numeric threshold with unit.

technology_references.note: Reference a specific technical standard or document instead of a relative quality claim.

forbidden_patterns.description: Word patterns structurally forbidden in requirement statements regardless of context.

patterns.note: Ambiguous conjunction — split into separate requirements or choose 'and' / 'or' explicitly.
Open-ended enumeration — list all items explicitly.
Open-ended enumeration — list all items explicitly.
Open-ended enumeration — list all items explicitly.
Undefined value — requirement is not ready for review.
Unconfirmed value — requirement is not ready for review.

sentence_morphology_bad_practices.description: Structural and grammatical patterns that impair clarity, verifiability, or unambiguity. Used by the LLM to detect morphological defects beyond term-level issues.

issues.double_negation: Use of two negations in the same clause (e.g. 'shall not be inactive'). Rewrite as a positive, measurable obligation.
issues.hidden_negation: Negative meaning expressed implicitly (e.g. 'unless otherwise specified'). Make the condition explicit.
issues.negative_requirement: Requirement expressed in negative form instead of a positive measurable behaviour. Prefer 'The X shall achieve Y' over 'The X shall not fail to achieve Y'.

issues.long_sentences: Sentences exceeding ~25 words. Split or restructure.
issues.multiple_subordinate_clauses: Stacked dependent clauses increasing cognitive load. Restructure using EARS patterns.
issues.nested_conditions: Multiple embedded IF/WHEN/WHILE structures. Decompose into separate requirements.
issues.compound_requirements: Several requirements combined with 'and' or 'or'. Split into one 'shall' per statement (REQ-R04).

issues.ambiguous_pronouns: Use of 'it', 'this', 'that', 'they' without a clear antecedent. Replace with the explicit subject.
issues.unclear_references: Reference to 'the system' when multiple systems are in scope. Name the specific system.
issues.dangling_modifiers: Modifier not clearly attached to the subject it qualifies.

issues.agentless_passive: Passive form without specifying the responsible entity (e.g. 'shall be processed'). Rewrite as '<Subject> shall <verb> <object>'.

issues.mixed_modal_verbs: Combination of 'shall', 'should', 'may', 'can' in the same requirement. Use a single, consistent modal.
issues.weak_modals: Use of 'should', 'may', 'can' instead of mandatory 'shall' for binding obligations (REQ-R03).

issues.and_or_combination: Use of 'and/or'. Choose one conjunction or split the requirement.
issues.implicit_conditions: Conditions not explicitly introduced by IF, WHEN, WHILE, or WHERE. Make them explicit.
issues.temporal_ambiguity: Unclear sequence of events (e.g. 'after initialisation'). Specify the exact trigger or duration.

issues.open_ended_lists: Use of 'etc.', 'including but not limited to'. Enumerate all items explicitly.
issues.ellipsis_or_incomplete_sentences: Sentence fragments — ensure the requirement is a complete, self-standing statement.

structural_rules.description: Explicit rule definitions for the pre-parser and structured checks (rule_id required).

rules.title: Single 'shall' per statement
rules.check: Count the number of 'shall' occurrences. More than one indicates a compound requirement.
rules.note: Split into separate requirements, one per obligation (REQ-R04).

rules.title: Subject explicitly stated
rules.check: Verify the grammatical subject of 'shall' is an identifiable system or function — not 'it', 'this', or omitted.
rules.note: The obligated entity must be named explicitly.

rules.title: No double or hidden negation
rules.check: Detect two negation markers in the same clause, or implicit negative constructions ('unless', 'except when').
rules.note: Rewrite as a positive, measurable obligation.

rules.title: No ambiguous pronouns
rules.check: Detect 'it', 'this', 'that', 'they', 'them' in the statement without a clear preceding antecedent.
rules.note: Replace with the explicit name of the system, component, or value.

rules.title: Sentence length
rules.check: Count words in the statement. Flag if count exceeds 30 words.
rules.note: Long sentences reduce clarity. Consider splitting or applying an EARS pattern.

ears_patterns.description: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) patterns for rewriting requirements. The recommender agent SHALL choose the most appropriate pattern based on the requirement's nature.
ears_patterns.reference: Mavin et al., EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), IEEE RE 2009.

patterns.name: Ubiquitous
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies always, unconditionally, with no trigger or precondition.
patterns.example: The Flight Control System shall respond to pilot inputs within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Event-Driven
patterns.template: WHEN <trigger> [<optional precondition>], the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement is triggered by a discrete event or stimulus.
patterns.example: WHEN the pilot applies a control input, the Flight Control System shall generate a surface deflection command within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Unwanted Behavior
patterns.template: IF <unwanted condition or event>, THEN the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement specifies the system's response to a fault, failure, or off-nominal condition.
patterns.example: IF a sensor failure is detected, THEN the Flight Control System shall switch to the redundant sensor within 50 ms.

patterns.name: State-Driven
patterns.template: WHILE <system state>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies continuously during a specific operating state or mode.
patterns.example: WHILE in degraded mode, the Flight Control System shall maintain attitude control with an accuracy of ±2°.

patterns.name: Optional Feature
patterns.template: WHERE <feature is included>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies only when an optional feature or configuration is present.
patterns.example: WHERE the enhanced autopilot feature is installed, the Flight Control System shall provide envelope protection.

patterns.name: Complex
patterns.template: (Combination of two or more EARS patterns above.)
patterns.use_when: The requirement involves multiple triggers, states, or conditions that cannot be cleanly separated without losing meaning.
patterns.example: WHILE in cruise mode, WHEN the autopilot is engaged, the Flight Control System shall maintain altitude within ±50 ft.
